message.abstract: <jats:sec><jats:title>Background</jats:title><jats:p>Glaucoma (GLAU), Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD), Retinal Vein Occlusion (RVO), and Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) are common blinding ophthalmic diseases worldwide.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Purpose</jats:title><jats:p>This approach is expected to enhance the early detection and treatment of common blinding ophthalmic diseases, contributing to the reduction of individual and economic burdens associated with these conditions.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Methods</jats:title><jats:p>We propose an effective deep-learning pipeline that combine both segmentation model and classification model for diagnosis and grading of four common blinding ophthalmic diseases and normal retinal fundus.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Results</jats:title><jats:p>In total, 102,786 fundus images of 75,682 individuals were used for training validation and external validation purposes. We test our model on internal validation data set, the micro Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUROC) of which reached 0.995. Then, we fine-tuned the diagnosis model to classify each of the four disease into early and late stage, respectively, which achieved AUROCs of 0.597 (GL), 0.877 (AMD), 0.972 (RVO), and 0.961 (DR) respectively. To test the generalization of our model, we conducted two external validation experiments on Neimeng and Guangxi cohort, all of which maintained high accuracy.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title><jats:p>Our algorithm demonstrates accurate artificial intelligence diagnosis pipeline for common blinding ophthalmic diseases based on Lesion-Focused fundus that overcomes the low-accuracy of the traditional classification method that based on raw retinal images, which has good generalization ability on diverse cases in different regions.</jats:p></jats:sec>
title: A deep-learning pipeline for the diagnosis and grading of common blinding ophthalmic diseases based on lesion-focused classification model
